count_gate.note: Question side labels 1-72 monotonic, no gaps, no duplicates (I 1-5, II 6-25, III 26-40, IV 41 (10-row table), V 42-51, VI 52-61, VII 62-66, VIII 67-71, IX 72). Answer side: keys 1-5 under the Lesson 3 heading are Lesson 4's MCQ keys (empty here + 'key belongs to another paper version'); keys 6-71 follow the question side, with '67.' printed three times (67 = q67; the second and third '67.' blocks are orphan keys); q72 unkeyed. The LBA prints no difficulty distribution table -> quota_table 'absent' (R-E6). Difficulty per question: easy 45, average 16, difficult 11, untagged 0.

method_notes: Pages: Q pdf 13 (heading, 10 LOs) 14-17; A 'Lesson – 3. Community' at the foot of pdf 75, keys 1-71 pdf 76-80.

Sections: s1 I mcq q1-5; s2 II fill q6-25; s3 III true/false q26-40; s4 IV match q41 (10 rows, '(Medium)'); s5 V one-mark vsa q42-51; s6 VI two-mark sa q52-61; s7 VII three-mark sa q62-66; s8 VIII four-mark la q67-71; s9 IX project work q72 sa.

SECTION I KEYS (control rev 2): the five keys printed under the Lesson 3 heading ('Enhances physical and mental health', 'Under extraordinary circumstances', 'Requires more preparation, speed, dexterity and training', 'Adventure games', 'Bachendri Pal') answer Lesson 4's MCQs and are printed again under 'Lesson 4' (pdf 81). Paired by printed number only: none names an option of q1-q5 -> option null + 'key belongs to another paper version' (pointer in the flag) + 'no answer printed' for this lesson's own key. Never re-paired by content.
q4 options print '(a)'..'(d)' on their own lines -> ids A-D. Other MCQs print 'A.'/'b.' or 'a)' labels.

KEY-SIDE LABEL '67.' printed three times (pdf 78-79): the first block answers q67; the second ('67. Lifestyle: …') carries q68's content; the third ('67. Differences: …') repeats key 62. Key 68 ('The three problems faced by the urban community are: …') repeats key 63 and adds 'Displacement from habitat'. q68 is paired by number to key 68 + 'key text does not address question' with a pointer; the two extra blocks are recorded in extraction.orphan_keys. Keys 69-71 fit their questions.
True/false keys restate the statement + '– Wrong' / '– Ok' -> label form, R-E4a doubted; q29 '– False' plain.

Match q41: column B on the question side is unlettered in the key; the key's rows 1/2 look swapped (flagged 'printed key contradicts fact', review-blocking). Key row 5 prints 'Shelter Scheme' for the question side's 'Ashraya Scheme' (translation) — left item taken from the question side.

Multi-line keys: one step per printed line/point; headings ending ':' on the number line (q67, q68, q69, q70) and inner sub-headings ('Types of community:', 'Problems:', 'Remedial measures:', 'Government measures:') are not steps. q71 essay = 3 printed paragraphs -> 3 steps.

TOPIC (R-E7): map v1 evs-5-03 s00 (Introduction, untickable), s01 'Different communities', s02 'Urban community', s03 'Tribal community'. Tagged by section title only: community in general, kinds of community, work-respect, interdependence -> s01 'high'; urban items -> s02; tribal items -> s03. Rural-community items (no section titled for them), rural-vs-urban comparisons and the mixed match table -> all three tickable sections 'low'. s00 never used. Mapping in the unit summary.

Transcription: c5auto.py rules (pdftotext -raw reading order; the rules of evs-5-01's hand transcription) + the overrides in build_03.py; every entry read against the layout text / renders before commit. Marks R-E5; difficulty Medium -> average (R-E2), Hard/Hardest -> difficult, printed word kept; LO = the lesson's printed list (R-E10); R-E4 flags in the 'unclassified — …' form (control rev 2 E1); topics R-E7 (mapping in the unit summary).

Value and interdependence of employment in the community Every person in the community is engaged in a different type of employment. Farmers produce food, doctors provide health care, teachers provide education. All such jobs are essential for the sustainability of the community.
Everyone should do their work with respect, regardless of whether any work is small or big. Employment increases the confidence of a person and instills intimacy in the society.
Through interdependence, we are all living directly or indirectly with each other's help. If the farmer is growing the crop, the trader sells it; Doctors take care of health. With such institutional cooperation, the community can be built greatly.

learning_outcomes.text_as_printed: Define what a community is in simple terms.
Identify various members/helpers of a community such as teachers, doctors, farmers, policemen, and sweepers.
Explain the roles and responsibilities of different people in a community.
Recognize the importance of living in a community and how people help one another.
Describe the services provided by the community like education, health care, safety, cleanliness, and food.
Develop respect for people who do various jobs in the community.
Understand the need for cooperation and unity among community members.
Give examples of how they contribute or can contribute to their own community (e.g., keeping surroundings clean).
Distinguish between different occupations and their contribution to society.
Demonstrate basic civic values like responsibility, cleanliness, and mutual support through classroom discussions and activities.
